parameters.content:
## SEO Agent — Pre-release Check (G27, v4.16)
`POST /webhook/seo-prerelease` (header auth: credential **SEO API Key**, header `X-API-Key`), synchronous (a few seconds), **free** — one plain GET per page plus `/robots.txt` per host, no paid API, nothing rendered.

Body: `{ base_url: 'https://staging.example.com', paths: ['/', '/pricing'] }` or `{ urls: ['https://staging.example.com/pricing'] }` (max 25), optional `live_host` (the address the pages will have in production) and `staging: false`.

Checks, the same ones the daily **Page Watch** runs on live key pages: does the page answer 200, does it redirect, is it `noindex`, does `robots.txt` allow it, one canonical pointing at the right page, one `<title>`, one H1, a meta description. On a staging host `noindex` and a robots.txt disallow are the deliberate staging guard, so they are **warnings** naming the live page; `staging: false` makes them failures.

**200** `{ ok, verdict: 'pass' | 'fail', exit_code: 0 | 1, summary, counts, failures: [{url, check, severity, detail}], warnings, not_checked: [{check, reason}], pages }` · **400** field errors (`exit_code: 2`).
CI in one line: `curl -s -H "X-API-Key: …" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @release.json $URL/webhook/seo-prerelease | jq -e '.exit_code == 0'`.

**It writes nothing** (`writes: "none"`): no Data Table node, no sub-workflow, so a release candidate never creates ladder rows, content-log rows or audits. What a staging host cannot answer — index coverage (Google has never crawled the URL), real-user speed (no Chrome visitors), positions — comes back as `not_checked` **with the reason**, never as "fine".
